# shift for pi and opencode

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@iiiokojiadbi/shift)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@iiiokojiadbi/shift)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@iiiokojiadbi/shift)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@iiiokojiadbi/shift)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@iiiokojiadbi/shift)](https://github.com/iiiokojiadbi/shift/blob/main/LICENSE)

The agent decides by itself when to **shift**. At a stage boundary it updates its work board and task folders, writes a letter to itself, and has the harness let the stretch's history go, with a direction of what to hold. Right after the shift it gets its letter, board, open track items and recent closures back and continues from where it stopped.

One package for both harnesses: pi loads `index.ts`, opencode loads `server.ts`.

```sh
pi install npm:@iiiokojiadbi/shift
opencode plugin add @iiiokojiadbi/shift
```

It adds a "Shift" section to the system prompt, the `shift` tool with its companions (`shift_guide`, `shift_status`, `shift_history`, `shift_setup`, `shift_sizes`, `task_open`, `task_track`, `task_archive`, `doc_outline`, `docs_mentioning`), and three commands: `/shift` asks the agent to shift now, `/shift-tasks` lists the open tasks, `/unshift` picks up the last shift in a fresh session. It hints a shift as the history grows.

The records live in the project's `.shift/` folder and stay out of its git unless `commit = true` in `.shift/settings.toml`.

How it works and why: [github.com/iiiokojiadbi/shift](https://github.com/iiiokojiadbi/shift).
